methods.boundary: A fixed unwinding string and a stationary rolling surface give a=R*alpha with signed conventions. A moving string end changes this constraint. During slip, kinetic friction and independent translation/rotation must be used instead. Preserve both CM and contact-origin derivations if explicitly requested.

methods.title: Transform vector time derivatives between rotating frames
methods.principle: Derivative of the rotating basis equals angular velocity cross basis
steps: Expand the vector in the rotating basis
Differentiate coefficients and basis vectors
Collect the angular-velocity cross product
Apply the identity again for acceleration when needed
Retain angular-acceleration terms if the rotation is not constant

methods.title: Choose a rotating frame to simplify a force law
methods.principle: Centrifugal or Coriolis cancellation against a real force
steps: Transform both velocity and acceleration into a frame with adjustable angular velocity
Collect position-dependent and velocity-dependent terms
Choose angular velocity to cancel the targeted term
Keep or explicitly estimate the remaining terms
Solve the reduced dynamics
Transform the result back to the original frame
methods.boundary: Discarding a residual magnetic-field-squared term is a weak-field approximation; exact oscillator centrifugal cancellation does not need that approximation.

methods.title: Compare one trajectory in inertial and rotating coordinates
methods.principle: Rotation matrix or complex phase transforms the same position vector
steps: Identify the initial velocity in each frame including frame rotation
Solve the simple inertial trajectory or use the supplied solution
Rotate its components into the other frame
Interpret shapes and limiting cases
Reconcile apparent bending with inertial forces

methods.title: Derive rotational energy and angular momentum in tensor form
methods.principle: Rigid velocity omega cross r and mass sums
steps: Insert the rigid rotational velocity into kinetic energy and angular momentum
Prove or apply the required vector-product identities
Sum mass-weighted terms into the inertia tensor
Obtain L=I omega and T=one-half omega dot L
Specialize to principal coordinates

methods.title: Relate axial angular momentum, inertia and angular speed
methods.principle: L_axis=I_axis*omega for the specified rigid rotation
steps: Choose the axis and identify whether spin or orbital angular momentum is requested
Compute the appropriate inertia or particle perpendicular lever arm
Evaluate signed angular momentum or invert it for the unknown angular speed
Use v=R*omega and period=2*pi/omega where requested
Check directional, dimensional and physical constraints
methods.boundary: General nonprincipal-axis rigid-body rotation requires the inertia tensor; the scalar formula alone does not determine the full angular momentum vector.

methods.title: Relate Coulomb impact parameter, scattering angle and detected counts
methods.principle: Repulsive inverse-square scattering maps incident area to outgoing solid angle
steps: State projectile charge, energy and heavy-target approximation
Use or derive the Coulomb relation between impact parameter and angle
For a cumulative threshold use the corresponding incident disk area
For angular bins differentiate the incident annulus and divide by outgoing solid angle
Multiply by incident flux, target areal density and detector acceptance as appropriate
Form ratios only after identifying which factors remain fixed
Check thin-target, screening and finite-size limits
methods.boundary: Counts above an angle scale with cotangent squared, whereas counts per solid angle scale with cosecant to the fourth. A requested Jacobian derivation must not be replaced by use of the finished formula.

methods.title: Follow sliding and spinning until rolling begins
methods.principle: Kinetic friction changes translation and rotation until contact slip vanishes
steps: Find the contact-point slip velocity from CM translation and spin
Choose kinetic friction opposite that slip and write force and central torque equations
Integrate the independent linear and angular accelerations from their initial values
Solve the first time that the contact velocity relative to the surface becomes zero
Evaluate CM distance and final speeds at that time
For energy loss include both translational and rotational changes, or integrate friction power at the slipping contact
methods.boundary: Do not impose v=R*omega before the transition. Friction times CM displacement alone is not the total work on a rotating body.

methods.title: Approximate motion near a stable potential minimum
methods.principle: Taylor expansion and curvature
steps: Locate the equilibrium by vanishing first derivative
Check positive second derivative
Expand the potential to quadratic order in displacement
Match its curvature and effective mass to the oscillator spring constant and frequency

methods.title: Derive hard-sphere scattering from specular reflection geometry
methods.principle: Equal incidence and reflection angles map impact parameter to outgoing angle
steps: Draw the surface normal at contact and define the impact parameter
Relate incidence angle to scattering angle
Express impact parameter through target radius and scattering angle
Convert the incident disk or annulus to cumulative or differential cross section
Multiply by incident intensity for a count rate
Check the zero-angle total geometric cross section
methods.boundary: The hard-sphere geometric reflection is distinct from continuous Coulomb deflection, even though both subsequently use the same area-to-angle mapping.

methods.title: Identify interaction pairs without cancelling forces on different bodies
methods.principle: Equal and opposite interaction forces act on different recipients
steps: Name the exerting and receiving object of each force
Reverse these roles to identify its third-law partner
Keep each partner on the appropriate separate free-body diagram
Distinguish interaction force from the net force on either object
Use the individual masses to compare accelerations when needed
methods.boundary: Two forces balancing on the same body are not a third-law pair; equal pair forces do not imply equal net force or acceleration.

methods.title: Reduce many-particle angular-momentum change to external torque
methods.principle: Central action-reaction pairs
steps: Differentiate the sum of position cross momentum
Eliminate velocity-cross-itself terms
Separate internal and external forces
Pair each internal action with its reaction
Use centrality to cancel the internal torque pair
Retain the external torque sum

methods.title: Use a supplied virial relation for a gravitational system
methods.principle: Equilibrated inverse-square gravity has potential energy=-2 kinetic energy
steps: Combine the supplied virial relation with total energy
Infer how kinetic energy responds to added total energy
Relate kinetic energy to temperature if a particle model is specified
Differentiate for heat capacity
Combine with a gravitational size-energy estimate when requested
methods.boundary: Using the theorem is not deriving the long-time theorem; a circular two-body example can be justified independently with radial force balance.

methods.title: Derive the long-time virial relation
methods.principle: Time derivative of position dot momentum
steps: Differentiate r dot p using Newton equations
Identify twice kinetic energy and r dot force
Integrate and divide by elapsed time
Use bounded endpoint terms for the long-time limit
Substitute the homogeneous potential derivative
methods.boundary: A circular-force balance is a special case but does not replace the requested time-average proof.

methods.title: Relate crystal diffraction peaks to wavelength and plane spacing
methods.principle: Constructive reflection requires a whole-wavelength path difference
steps: Identify the crystalline plane spacing and angle convention
Use twice spacing times sine of the glancing angle equals order times wavelength
Check whether the requested order is geometrically possible
Compare peak angles or infer wavelength
For particles convert wavelength to momentum or accelerating energy
methods.boundary: Replacing photons by particles with the same wavelength preserves the kinematic Bragg angles, not necessarily the scattering strengths.

methods.title: Derive reflection or refraction from a stationary interface point
methods.principle: Sum of travel times to and from a variable interface point
steps: Parameterize the reflection or crossing point on the interface
Express both segment lengths and their refractive-index weights
Differentiate total travel time with respect to each interface coordinate
Obtain coplanarity and the angular condition
Check the stationary point type on the allowed domain

methods.title: Explain laser gain, inversion and coherence
methods.principle: Stimulated emission amplifies a field when gain exceeds absorption and loss
steps: Identify upper and lower laser states and the pump pathway
Explain how population inversion relative to their degeneracies is sustained
Relate stimulated emission to the incident mode and frequency
Identify feedback or amplification geometry
Distinguish phase coherence from narrow bandwidth
Compare with thermal spontaneous emission
methods.boundary: A metastable upper state is useful in the textbook laser model, not an absolute requirement for every laser architecture. Population inversion concerns the laser transition, not necessarily a majority of all atoms in one state.

methods.title: Explain material transmission, reflection, absorption or color
methods.principle: Observed light combines source spectrum with material-dependent absorption, reflection and scattering
steps: Identify the illuminating or self-emitted spectrum
Determine which wavelengths are absorbed, transmitted or scattered
Relate the surviving spectrum to the transmitted signal or, for visible light, perceived color
Distinguish transparency from merely weak visible absorption
Compare the required electronic or structural response
For a conducting radio shield,identify the driven currents and retain the scale of openings relative to wavelength
methods.boundary: Blackbody thermal emission, selective reflection and a colored line-emission flame must not be treated as the same mechanism.

methods.title: Estimate diffraction-limited resolving angle
methods.principle: Finite aperture spreads a point image into a diffraction pattern
steps: Identify aperture geometry and wavelength
Use the appropriate first-minimum angular scale
Apply the specified resolution criterion
Convert between angle and object separation if needed
Compare how aperture or wavelength changes resolution
methods.boundary: A smaller resolving angle means better resolving power. The ideal diffraction limit does not include real lens aberrations.

methods.title: Imaginary potential, probability loss and lifetime
methods.principle: Non-Hermitian Schrodinger evolution
steps: Differentiate the total norm and substitute V = V0 - i Gamma and its conjugate.
Retain the imaginary-potential loss term after cancellation of boundary flux.
Solve the resulting first-order decay equation and identify the exponential lifetime.
methods.boundary: Additional imaginary potential destroys the real-potential conservation result.

methods.title: Prove angular-momentum addition ranges and multiplicities
methods.principle: Triangle rule and finite multiplet sums
steps: Apply the two-body triangle rule to each intermediate angular momentum
Take the union of allowed final ranges while retaining repeated multiplets
Derive endpoint bounds or sum their 2j+1 dimensions
Use induction to compare with the product-state dimension

methods.title: Estimate departures from instantaneous adiabatic following
methods.principle: Time derivatives of instantaneous eigenstates
steps: Obtain the level gap and the off-diagonal derivative coupling
Compare variation time with the inverse gap frequency
Integrate the derivative coupling with its dynamical phase and actual turn-on boundary
Square the amplitude for the requested excitation probability
Multiply by ensemble size when a particle count is requested
methods.boundary: A local derivative estimate must not discard a finite turn-on boundary contribution without justification.

methods.title: Track an eigenstate under slow parameter variation
methods.principle: Adiabatic following of a gapped level
steps: Identify the initial eigenstate branch
Check the slow variation relative to relevant gaps
Replace parameters in the instantaneous eigenstate and eigenenergy without changing branch labels
Include dynamical or geometric phases only if the requested output requires them
Subtract endpoint energies for quasistatic work

methods.title: Adjoints and Hermiticity by inner products
methods.principle: Conjugate symmetry, integration by parts and operator order
steps: Move each factor across the inner product by conjugation or integration by parts
Retain endpoint terms and state the boundary assumption
Reverse the order in a product
Compare with the original operator or matrix to find the Hermiticity condition
methods.boundary: Checking formal Hermiticity is not a full self-adjoint domain classification; that additional task is separate.

methods.title: Prove spectral consequences of Hermiticity or anti-Hermiticity
methods.principle: Adjoint identity on eigenvectors
steps: Compare an expectation with its conjugate using the adjoint sign
Apply that relation to an eigenvector to constrain the eigenvalue
Apply it between two eigenvectors to prove orthogonality for distinct eigenvalues

methods.title: Linear-potential bound states above a hard floor
methods.principle: Airy reduction and hard-wall quantization
steps: Nondimensionalize the linear-potential stationary equation
Select the decaying Airy branch
Impose a zero at the hard floor and find the required roots
Normalize and plot eigenfunctions
Check orthogonality with their overlap

methods.title: Diagnose the angle-angular-momentum uncertainty paradox
methods.principle: Operator domains and endpoint terms on a periodic interval
steps: Evaluate the formal angle commutator
Compute the finite angle variance on the chosen branch interval
Compare the naive uncertainty claim with an angular-momentum eigenstate
Inspect periodic-domain preservation or the boundary term to locate the failed hypothesis
methods.boundary: This diagnoses why a bound cannot be used; it is not an ordinary Robertson application.

methods.title: Derive angular-momentum ladder coefficients
methods.principle: Adjoint ladder relation and norm preservation
steps: Express the squared raised or lowered norm as an expectation of the ordered opposite ladders
Replace their product by J squared and Jz terms
Insert the eigenvalues
Take the positive magnitude and check top/bottom termination

methods.title: Read scattering coefficients from a supplied exact state
methods.principle: Asymptotic traveling-wave decomposition and probability flux
steps: Take left and right asymptotic limits of the supplied scattering solution
Identify incident, reflected and transmitted amplitudes and wavenumbers
Form current ratios and interpret reflectionlessness or conservation
methods.boundary: No interface-matching equations are needed.

methods.title: Enumerate atomic LS terms with equivalent-electron exclusion
methods.principle: Antisymmetric microstate counting
steps: List distinct occupations of the available magnetic spin orbitals or equivalent holes
Tabulate total ML and MS
Remove complete LS multiplets from highest remaining projections
Enumerate their J values
Verify the total microstate dimension
methods.boundary: Simply adding distinguishable angular momenta produces forbidden extra terms for equivalent electrons.

methods.title: Relate a spherical harmonic to the correct quantization axis
methods.principle: Meaning of polar and azimuthal coordinates
steps: Identify the polar axis defining theta and phi
Identify which Cartesian component generates rotations about that axis
Distinguish rotationally invariant J-squared from the axis-dependent component
State how rotating the axes changes the component eigenbasis

methods.title: Derive or perform a basis change using completeness
methods.principle: Complete orthogonal resolutions of the identity
steps: Insert the stated complete basis into the vector or on each side of the operator
Take overlaps with the desired basis vectors
Use orthogonality to contract intermediate labels
Divide by basis norms where the basis is orthogonal but not normalized
Collect the coefficient sum,integral or two-sided matrix transformation with a consistent adjoint convention
For a supplied transformation,evaluate the same contracted matrix products and check the claimed diagonal entries without re-solving for eigenvectors
methods.boundary: Numerically evaluating an overlap is covered separately. Proving a supplied overlap matrix is unitary adds its matrix-product identity.

methods.title: Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula for a central commutator
methods.principle: Commutator induction and uniqueness of an operator ODE
steps: Prove the power commutator by induction under the stated commuting-commutator assumption
Sum the power series to commute an exponential
Differentiate the candidate factorized exponential
Show both forms obey the same first-order equation and initial value
methods.boundary: The exponential factorization proof is more than evaluating one elementary commutator.

methods.title: Quantize a circular,cylindrical or spherical hard-wall radial state
methods.principle: Regular radial Bessel solution and a zero at the wall
steps: Separate the stated radial geometry and identify its Bessel order and measure
Discard the irregular origin branch
Set the regular branch to zero at the wall
Locate the required root and convert its wave number to energy
Compare branches and derive any requested large-root limit
methods.boundary: Finite outside barriers require derivative matching and decay,not a hard-wall zero.

methods.title: Verify Bloch form of a perturbed plane wave
methods.principle: Reciprocal-lattice Fourier harmonics
steps: Factor the common plane wave from the supplied perturbation expansion
Express the remainder as reciprocal-lattice harmonics
Shift position by one lattice period
Show every remaining harmonic is unchanged
methods.boundary: No new eigenvalue calculation is needed when the corrected expansion is supplied.

methods.title: Interpret a wavefunction, probability density and expectation
methods.principle: Squared amplitude gives probability density, not a classical trajectory
steps: Identify the spatial dimension and probability measure
Distinguish a complex amplitude from its nonnegative modulus squared
Infer units from normalization
Interpret interval probabilities and ensemble expectations
Distinguish a density node from a statement about a classical crossing trajectory
methods.boundary: An expectation need not be an individual measured eigenvalue or the most probable result. Probability at a mathematical point is zero for any continuous distribution, independently of whether its density is zero there.

methods.title: Sketch bound-state shapes using curvature,nodes and boundaries
methods.principle: The stationary equation fixes curvature sign through V-E
steps: Sketch the potential and mark the classically allowed region and turning points for the stated energy
Use psi-double-prime proportional to(V-E)*psi to distinguish oscillatory and forbidden-region curvature
Impose hard-wall zeros or continuity and smooth matching at finite steps
Use parity when justified and order the ground and excited states by their nodes
Draw decaying tails and the corresponding squared density when requested
Check every qualitative feature without claiming numerical eigenvalues from an educated sketch
methods.boundary: A requested qualitative sketch does not require solving an Airy or finite-well transcendental equation. Exact eigenvalues and normalized wavefunctions are separate tasks when requested.

methods.title: Apply the known hard-box energy and standing-wave spectrum
methods.principle: Positive-integer box energies scale as n squared over mass times length squared
steps: Identify the box length,particle mass and correct positive integer level index
Use E_n=n squared*pi squared*hbar squared/(2mL squared) and the corresponding standing-wave wavelength
Evaluate or invert the level energy,gap,length or quantum number
For a changed size or mass form the corresponding scaling ratio
For a limiting argument compare the absolute or fractional spacing with the stated physical scale
Check the positive-integer,nonrelativistic and infinite-wall assumptions
methods.boundary: This uses the established box spectrum. Solving the wave equation and enforcing both wall conditions to derive the spectrum is separately listed;constructing a photon from an energy gap is cross-listed when requested.

methods.title: Compute bras, inner products and outer-product matrices
methods.principle: Complex conjugation and basis expansion
steps: Conjugate coefficients to form the dual bra
Contract matching orthonormal basis indices for inner products
Form the column-times-conjugate-row matrix for an outer product
Compare entries with the conjugate transpose if Hermiticity is requested

methods.title: Obtain the overlap of ideal canonical-conjugate eigenstates
methods.principle: Derivative representation of a regular canonical pair
steps: Choose the representation in which one observable multiplies its coordinate
Represent its regular canonical conjugate by a derivative
Solve the other eigenvalue equation for the overlap kernel
Read its constant modulus and continuum normalization
Inspect domain and periodic-endpoint assumptions
methods.boundary: A formal commutator alone does not license this regular representation on every domain; the angle variable requires the separate domain check.

methods.title: Complete a commuting set using intermediate angular momenta
methods.principle: Nested partial-total angular-momentum Casimirs
steps: Choose nested subsets of the constituent angular momenta
Form the squared partial totals
Show their commutators vanish with total J-squared, total Jz and individual magnitudes
Check mutual commutation and independence of the additional labels
methods.boundary: Commuting with the original operators alone does not prove the new operators commute with each other; arbitrary overlapping-subset combinations need this extra check.

methods.title: Rescale the Coulomb spectrum to another inverse-radius interaction
methods.principle: Identical dimensionless central eigenvalue equation
steps: Identify the new attractive coupling and particle or reduced mass
Substitute them into the length and energy scales
Read corresponding binding energies and spectral constants
Interpret the physical regime without resolving the differential equation

methods.title: Construct coupled angular-momentum states
methods.principle: Total ladders, normalization and orthogonality
steps: Fix total projection and list the allowed product states
Start from a highest-weight state or impose the total-J-squared eigenvalue equation
Determine coefficients by ladder action or the resulting finite linear system
Normalize and construct orthogonal remaining multiplets
Check phase convention and any tabulated examples
methods.boundary: Deriving coefficients is not replaced by looking them up.

methods.title: Use Clebsch-Gordan coefficients for a basis change or measurement
methods.principle: Coupled and uncoupled angular-momentum bases
steps: Identify the two constituent spins and the conserved total projection
Select the appropriate table row/column with its sign convention
Expand the state in the measurement basis
Square amplitudes and sum over unobserved labels for the requested outcome

methods.title: Reduce a sum of matrix-element products by completeness
methods.principle: Resolution of the identity
steps: Write matrix elements as bra-operator-ket products
Use Hermiticity where a modulus squared is present
Insert the complete sum of intermediate projectors
Collapse the sum to the identity
Evaluate the resulting operator product or moment

methods.title: Construct and analyze an oscillator coherent state
methods.principle: Annihilation-operator eigenvalue equation
steps: Use the eigenvalue and adjoint relations to compute ladder moments
Expand in number states and match coefficients recursively
Normalize the resulting exponential series
Attach oscillator energy phases and identify the evolving eigenvalue
Derive means, fixed widths and the minimum-uncertainty property

methods.title: Relate commutation to a complete common eigenbasis
methods.principle: Linearity and completeness
steps: Act with both ordered operator products on each common eigenvector
Show the commutator annihilates each basis vector
Expand an arbitrary vector in the complete basis
Conclude the operator identity or its contrapositive

methods.title: Evaluate operator commutators algebraically
methods.principle: Product rule and canonical commutation relations
steps: Expand commutators and apply the sum/product identities without reordering noncommuting factors
Reduce elementary commutators
Extend powers by induction or an analytic function by its series
Simplify the resulting operator expression

methods.title: Prove simultaneous diagonalization of commuting Hermitian matrices
methods.principle: Invariant degenerate eigenspaces
steps: Diagonalize the first Hermitian operator
Use commutation to show the second preserves each degenerate eigenspace
Diagonalize the second within those blocks
Assemble a common orthonormal basis
Prove the converse by multiplying diagonal forms
methods.boundary: The degenerate-block construction is additional to the simpler proof that a complete common eigenbasis implies commutation.

methods.title: Evolve a time-dependent Hamiltonian with a fixed eigenbasis
methods.principle: Decoupled first-order amplitude equations
steps: Express the Hamiltonian in its fixed eigenbasis
Integrate each time-dependent eigenvalue in its phase
Fix amplitudes from the initial state
Recombine and project for requested probabilities or inversion conditions
methods.boundary: Do not use constant-energy stationary phases for a varying field; no time ordering is needed only because the Hamiltonians commute at different times.

methods.title: Derive norm/overlap conservation and boundary flux
methods.principle: Schrodinger equation with a common real potential
steps: Differentiate a bilinear wavefunction product or its integral.
Substitute the equation and conjugate, cancel the common real potential.
Write the remaining derivative as a boundary flux by the product rule/integration by parts.
Evaluate at finite endpoints or vanishing infinity to obtain the conservation statement.
methods.boundary: The same ordered steps cover an overlap of two solutions and the single-state probability case; evaluating a supplied current is separate.

methods.title: Identify unchanged states and observables under a common energy or phase shift
methods.principle: Schrodinger equation and bilinear observables
steps: For H shifted by a scalar identity term,apply it to an original eigenstate and identify the shifted energy without changing the eigenfunction
For the corresponding time dependence,differentiate the common time phase and match the energy offset
Cancel that common phase against its conjugate in probabilities or expectation integrands
For a constant perturbation,orthogonality makes off-diagonal elements vanish,so perturbative eigenfunction corrections vanish as well
Distinguish this unobservable common phase from measurable relative phases or beat frequencies between different energies
methods.boundary: A spatially varying potential is not a common scalar shift. A single stationary-state global frequency is not directly observable;phase differences and energy differences can be measured.

methods.title: Explain the classical limit of a quantum system
methods.principle: Relative quantum spacings and coarse-grained distributions approach classical behavior in the appropriate regime
steps: Identify the energy or action scale compared with Planck constant
Compare neighboring level spacings with the system energy
Compare quantum probability with a suitably coarse-grained classical distribution
Explain why a classical approximation suffices for the stated macroscopic measurement
Keep the small-system or low-energy exceptions
methods.boundary: Large quantum number does not by itself replace every coherent quantum phenomenon by classical dynamics; state the observable and resolution implicit in the comparison.

methods.title: Evaluate a two-center-coordinate Coulomb integral for spherical densities
methods.principle: Angular expansion of inverse separation
steps: Write the two-particle density and both volume measures
Expand inverse separation or use the shell average
Perform angular integrations
Split radial integration into r1<r2 and r1>r2
Evaluate the remaining radial integrals

methods.title: Find angular-momentum dot products and coupled-spin energies through total squares
methods.principle: Two A dot B equals (A+B) squared minus A squared minus B squared
steps: Rewrite the pair couplings in total or compatible subgroup angular-momentum squares
Enumerate the allowed constituent,intermediate and total angular momenta
Insert j*(j+1)*hbar squared for each squared magnitude
Evaluate dot products or their stated energy coefficients
If a ground state is requested,compare all allowed combinations and count its multiplet degeneracy
methods.boundary: Deriving a radial coupling coefficient is additional. Arbitrary overlapping pair couplings need not have simultaneous total-square eigenstates;do not assume this reduction diagonalizes every spin network.

methods.title: Derive the strengthened covariance uncertainty relation
methods.principle: Cauchy-Schwarz without dropping the real part
steps: Form centered-observable vectors
Apply Cauchy-Schwarz
Separate the squared complex overlap into real and imaginary parts
Identify the anticommutator covariance and commutator terms
Check the specified coincident-observable case

methods.title: Evaluate probability current from a supplied state
methods.principle: J = (hbar/m) Im(psi* dpsi/dx)
steps: Differentiate the specified spatial wavefunction.
Form its conjugate-gradient product and extract the imaginary part.
Interpret sign, units and flux or vanishing current.
methods.boundary: Does not derive the continuity theorem.

methods.title: Test source freedom of a superposed particle current
methods.principle: Bilinear current and cross terms
steps: Expand the current of the sum into two diagonal currents and cross currents
Take the divergence
Cancel gradient cross terms
Use the given imaginary-part condition to test whether a cross-term source remains

methods.title: Count allowed quantum-number states under a stated constraint
methods.principle: Allowed quantum numbers and spectral multiplicity
steps: Write the stated energy,angular-quantum-number or shell constraint and all allowed quantum-number ranges
Enumerate or count all ordered allowed tuples or angular multiplets satisfying it
Include permutation and magnetic multiplicities once
Identify accidental coincidences between different tuples

methods.title: Update a state after a partial or degenerate measurement
methods.principle: Projection onto the full measured eigenspace
steps: Identify every compatible eigenstate sharing the measured eigenvalue
Project the initial amplitudes onto that full subspace
Retain coherence between its unmeasured labels
Normalize by the selected-outcome probability
Evolve the surviving components if requested
methods.boundary: Measuring one momentum component does not measure the full vector or select an arbitrary single plane wave.

methods.title: Bound states with delta-potential matching
methods.principle: Continuity plus derivative jump from a delta potential
steps: Solve the free equation in each interval with decaying tails or stated hard walls
Use parity where available
Impose continuity and the delta-induced derivative jump at each spike
Solve/count the energy roots and examine wavefunctions and limiting cases

methods.title: Recover delta-potential results as a shrinking square-well limit
methods.principle: Fixed-area singular limit
steps: Relate well depth and width while holding integrated strength fixed
Expand the finite-well bound/scattering equations in the shrinking-width limit
Retain the finite leading terms and compare with delta results
methods.boundary: This requested asymptotic derivation is not direct interface matching.

methods.title: Scattering through delta potentials
methods.principle: Incident/outgoing waves and delta derivative jumps
steps: Write incident, reflected and transmitted traveling waves in each interval
Impose continuity and the derivative jump at every spike
Solve for amplitude ratios
Take outgoing-to-incoming current ratios for reflection and transmission
methods.boundary: Transfer-matrix composition is separately listed when explicitly requested.

methods.title: Construct a density matrix and compute ensemble expectations
methods.principle: Weighted projectors and trace expectation
steps: Specify pure member kets and their ensemble weights
Sum the weighted outer products without deleting known coherences
Check Hermiticity, positivity and unit trace
Evaluate the requested expectation or probability by a trace
Distinguish unspecified off-diagonal entries from known zero entries

methods.title: Distinguish a pure superposition from an incoherent mixture
methods.principle: Rank-one projectors and coherence
steps: Determine whether amplitudes and relative phases are specified or only populations
Form the corresponding projector or ensemble density
Compare coherences and evaluate purity or rank if needed
Explain which measurements the given information fixes
methods.boundary: Equal populations in one measurement basis do not imply equal density matrices.

methods.title: Find eigenvalues and normalized eigenvectors of a finite Hermitian matrix
methods.principle: Matrix eigenvalue equation
steps: Construct matrix entries from the given basis if needed
Solve the characteristic equation using block structure when available
Solve each eigenvector nullspace
Orthonormalize degenerate subspaces and normalize the eigenvectors
methods.boundary: Measurement probabilities and time evolution are additional tasks if requested, not implicit requirements of diagonalization.

methods.title: Derive dipole selection rules from angular matrix elements
methods.principle: Spherical-harmonic recurrences and orthogonality
steps: Express dipole components as r cos(theta) or r sin(theta) exp(plus/minus i phi)
Reduce the angular product using harmonic recurrences
Apply azimuthal and polar orthogonality
Identify surviving changes in magnetic and orbital labels
methods.boundary: Deriving the rules is distinct from applying a provided rule to a level diagram.

methods.title: Time evolution and measurements in a discrete energy basis
methods.principle: Spectral expansion and stationary phase factors
steps: Normalize and obtain the expansion coefficients in the fixed energy basis
Multiply each coefficient by exp(-i E_n t/hbar)
Reconstruct the state and retain interference terms for density or position observables
Use squared energy-basis coefficients for energy probabilities and weighted energy means
methods.boundary: A common overall phase cancels; relative phases and multistate interference must remain.

methods.title: Qualitative bonding and splitting in a double well
methods.principle: Parity, node ordering and overlap of localized states
steps: Compare coincident, moderately separated and isolated wells
Sketch even ground and odd first-excited combinations with correct nodes
Infer energy splitting and its separation dependence
Infer attraction/repulsion from the energy trend
methods.boundary: The source expressly prohibits calculations; it is not a quantitative matching exercise.

methods.title: Derive expectation-value evolution
methods.principle: Time-dependent Schrodinger equation
steps: Differentiate the expectation integral including both wavefunction factors.
Substitute the Schrodinger equation and its conjugate (equivalently evaluate the Hamiltonian commutator).
Integrate by parts with vanishing boundary terms; simplify to the mean-force/evolution relation.
methods.boundary: Derivation, not merely applying the already known classical-looking relation.

methods.title: Check mean motion against Ehrenfest relations
methods.principle: Ehrenfest relations for already computed expectations
steps: Find the time-dependent position and momentum means from the supplied state
Differentiate those means
Compare with the mean force computed from the potential
methods.boundary: Checks a particular state, rather than deriving the general theorem.

methods.title: Verify an eigenstate or eigenspace
methods.principle: Linear eigenvalue equation
steps: Apply the given operator to the proposed function or linear combination
Compare the result with a constant multiple of that same vector
Identify its eigenvalue or explain failure
Use linearity to describe combinations within a degenerate eigenspace

methods.title: Obtain a spontaneous-emission coefficient from a dipole matrix element
methods.principle: Einstein coefficient ratio and radiation-density convention
steps: Identify whether the given B coefficient uses ordinary or angular frequency density
Combine B with the matching equilibrium A-over-B relation
Insert the dipole-matrix formula and isotropic polarization factor
Convert frequency conventions consistently
Check the cubic-frequency scaling

methods.title: Verify then reject a singular angular solution
methods.principle: Differential equation and physical endpoint conditions
steps: Differentiate the proposed solution and verify the angular equation away from the poles
Examine the polar limits and operator boundary behavior
Explain the violated admissibility condition
methods.boundary: Do not claim its norm diverges merely because its value diverges: the logarithmic example has an integrable squared norm with the angular measure.

methods.title: Bound-state energy lower bound from normalizability
methods.principle: Curvature of a stationary Schrodinger solution
steps: Assume energy does not exceed the potential minimum
Compare the signs of the function and its curvature
Show that the resulting nonzero solution cannot obey normalizable boundary behavior
State the classical kinetic-energy counterpart

methods.title: Evaluate an observable-dependent energy-time uncertainty
methods.principle: Variance and rate-of-change time scale
steps: Calculate energy mean and variance in the supplied state
Calculate the chosen observable variance and the time derivative of its mean
Form delta t as sigma Q over the absolute rate
Test sigma H times delta t against hbar/2 and interpret stationary-rate limits

methods.title: Explain exchange-symmetry energy ordering and bonding
methods.principle: Antisymmetry and the spatial charge distribution
steps: Infer spatial symmetry from the spin sector
Identify enhanced overlap or a coincidence node
Compare electron repulsion and electron-nuclear attraction in that distribution
Infer the energy ordering or whether the supplied potential curve has a bound minimum
methods.boundary: An exchange correlation is not a new classical force; helium level ordering and molecular binding balance different Coulomb contributions.

methods.title: Prove the two-spin exchange operator identity
methods.principle: Action on a complete product basis
steps: Apply the proposed operator to each product-basis ket using spin ladders
Compare with exchange of the particle labels
Conclude equality by basis completeness
Rewrite the spin dot product through the total spin square
methods.boundary: This verifies an exchange operator rather than minimizing energies of an exchange-coupled Hamiltonian.

methods.title: Construct free partial waves outside a hard sphere
methods.principle: Exterior spherical Bessel solutions and a contact boundary
steps: Separate center-of-mass and relative motion
Write both spherical Bessel and Neumann branches on the exterior domain
Impose zero relative wavefunction at the hard-core radius
Determine the branch ratio and continuous energy label
State the angular parity
methods.boundary: The origin is excluded; do not discard the Neumann branch or impose interior-well discrete quantization.

methods.title: Construct a two-state nilpotent ladder and its number projector
methods.principle: Nilpotence and canonical anticommutation
steps: Expand the proposed number-operator square
Replace the reversed ladder product using the anticommutator
Cancel nilpotent terms to prove idempotence
Choose a two-state lowering matrix and verify the defining identities

methods.title: Fill lowest one-particle states under the stated occupancy rule
methods.principle: Pauli exclusion and an ordered single-particle spectrum
steps: Specify the allowed levels,spin multiplicities and bosonic or fermionic occupancy restriction
Fill the lowest states up to the required particle number
Sum their energies
Compare configurations or take a large-number limit for binding energy
methods.boundary: Fermions occupy distinct one-particle spin states;identical bosons can share the lowest state. If the source explicitly ignores spin,use its stated occupancy model rather than silently restoring spin degeneracy.

methods.title: Piecewise finite-well bound states
methods.principle: Stationary equation and interface continuity
steps: Choose oscillatory interior and decaying exterior solutions with any hard-wall condition
Enforce continuity of the wavefunction and derivative at finite interfaces
Eliminate amplitudes to get the energy equation
Count/find roots graphically or numerically and examine limiting cases
methods.boundary: Normalizing an already supplied solution requires density integration, not re-solving the spectrum.

methods.title: Finite-difference Hamiltonian eigenvalues and grid refinement
methods.principle: Discretized stationary Schrodinger equation
steps: Choose the grid and impose boundary values
Replace the second derivative by the three-point stencil and add the potential diagonal
Diagonalize the resulting matrix analytically for tiny grids or numerically
Compare eigenvalues/eigenvectors across grid resolution and against any known spectrum
methods.boundary: A matrix-eigenvalue algorithm, not shooting.

methods.title: One-dimensional finite-interface scattering and flux
methods.principle: Stationary wave matching and probability current
steps: Choose traveling, evanescent or linear solutions in each region according to energy relative to the potential
Set the incoming boundary condition
Match the wavefunction and its derivative at each finite interface

methods.boundary: An unread spin sum is not the squared sum of its spatial amplitudes.

methods.title: Finite spin-state normalization, moments and uncertainty
methods.principle: Spin matrices and normalized complex spinors
steps: Normalize the coefficient vector
Evaluate chi-dagger S_i chi and chi-dagger S_i-squared chi
Subtract squared means to form variances
Check a requested commutator uncertainty relation or its equality condition
methods.boundary: This is finite-dimensional operator expectation algebra; matrix construction and diagonalization are extra tasks only when the matrices/bases are not supplied.

methods.title: Find spin-orbit energy shifts of a hydrogenic multiplet
methods.principle: First-order expectation of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian
steps: Identify n, l, s and allowed j values
Write the spin-orbit Hamiltonian with its Thomas factor
Evaluate its radial inverse-cube expectation for l greater than zero
Replace L dot S by half the difference of angular-momentum squares
Compare the j branches and distinguish this correction from the full relativistic fine structure
methods.boundary: An s state has zero orbital spin-orbit term, not the divergent l-to-zero limit of the inverse-cube formula. Full fine structure also contains other terms.

methods.title: Find or exclude a pure spin state with prescribed mean components
methods.principle: Spinor amplitudes and moment equations
steps: Parameterize a normalized pure state by complex amplitudes
Evaluate the specified component means
Solve or compare the amplitude and phase constraints
Supply a nonzero normalized example or show a contradiction
methods.boundary: Spin-one and spin-half may yield different existence answers; do not infer a mixed state merely from zero vector polarization in every spin dimension.

methods.title: Predict Stern-Gerlach beam selection and separation
methods.principle: A magnetic-moment projection acquires a force in a field gradient
steps: Determine the total electronic angular momentum and its allowed magnetic projections
Relate each projection to its magnetic moment in the stated coupling regime
Obtain the transverse force from the field gradient
Integrate acceleration through the magnet and free drift to the detector
Identify the outgoing spin-conditioned spatial beams and distinguish a mixed input from a pure superposition
methods.boundary: Multiplicity is not generally determined by spin alone; open-shell orbital moment and the coupling regime matter. Ignore nuclear hyperfine structure only when specified or within the textbook model.

methods.title: Construct supersymmetric partner potentials
methods.principle: First-order Hamiltonian factorization
steps: Expand the two ordered factor products including the derivative of W
Read the partner potentials
Prove eigenstate intertwining by associativity
Use ground-state annihilation to express W as a logarithmic derivative
Evaluate the specified partner, retaining distributional derivatives at cusps

methods.title: Construct symmetry-adapted stationary solutions
methods.principle: Linearity and invariance of the real stationary equation
steps: Apply conjugation or reflection and check that the transformed function solves the same eigenvalue equation
Form the symmetric and antisymmetric linear combinations
Identify the resulting real or definite-parity basis
methods.boundary: A symmetry proof, not a numerical eigenstate calculation.

methods.title: Construct the scattering matrix from two-sided incidence
methods.principle: Linearity of scattering amplitudes
steps: Write outgoing amplitudes as linear functions of independent left/right incoming amplitudes
Solve each incidence case with the proper boundary/jump conditions or exploit a verified symmetry
Place reflected/transmitted amplitudes into the S-matrix
Relate entries to the specified flux probabilities

methods.title: Apply a total-spin operator on a product state
methods.principle: Operators act on their own tensor factors
steps: Expand the total operator into single-particle terms or ladder products
Act on the appropriate tensor factor without altering the other
Collect product-state amplitudes
Compare with the claimed eigenvector or target coupled state

methods.title: Construct independent-coordinate or independent-subsystem quantum product states
methods.principle: A sum of independent Hamiltonians has tensor-product eigenstates and additive energies
steps: Identify the independent coordinates or subsystems and their one-factor Hamiltonians
Separate the equation or use the stated one-factor eigenbases with their boundary conditions
Form the product of the spatial,spin or number-state factors
List all independent labels and add the corresponding eigenenergies
Attach the requested common stationary-state time phase
Count product dimensions or enumerate coincident summed energies when requested
methods.boundary: An interaction coupling factors invalidates this separation. Indistinguishable-particle symmetrization,ladder action and degeneracy enumeration are separately listed when requested. Spin populations alone do not fix a pure spinor.

methods.title: Translate angular quantum numbers and spectroscopic terms
methods.principle: LS addition rule and term notation
steps: Read or assign L from the orbital letter and S from the multiplicity
Enumerate J from the triangle range if needed
Write or decode the term subscript
Distinguish spin multiplicity 2S+1 from the number of J levels when L<S

methods.title: Calculate weak time-dependent transition probabilities
methods.principle: First-order interaction-picture amplitude
steps: Identify the initial and final unperturbed states and energy difference
Evaluate the spatial or spin perturbation matrix element including selection-rule zeros
Integrate its time envelope times the energy-gap phase over the actual application interval
Square the amplitude with the proper hbar factor
Apply the requested resonance or pulse-duration limit
Check that the transition probability remains perturbatively small
methods.boundary: Gaussian, exponential and sinusoidal envelopes use the same amplitude construction but different elementary integrals; exact large-amplitude Rabi dynamics is not this approximation.

methods.title: Transfer-matrix conversion and composition
methods.principle: Linear amplitude relations across successive regions
steps: Rearrange S relations into left-to-right transfer form
Construct or translate each element matrix with its propagation phases
Multiply matrices in spatial order
Read the reflection/transmission ratios from the combined matrix
methods.boundary: Composition is an additional method beyond a single potential S-matrix.

methods.title: Apply a known step or barrier transmission and attenuation law
methods.principle: Flux coefficients and evanescent attenuation for the specified one-dimensional potential
steps: Identify the step or barrier geometry,particle mass,energy and potential difference
Calculate propagating wave numbers or the evanescent decay constant with consistent units
Choose the appropriate supplied exact coefficient or explicitly justified opaque-barrier approximation
Evaluate,invert or compare reflection,transmission or the specified normalized evanescent density
For currents or counts include the stated incident flux and use probabilities rather than amplitudes
Check velocity weighting,conservation,the nonrelativistic regime and whether an exponential approximation is controlled
methods.boundary: Deriving the coefficient by solving interface equations is separately listed. Amplitude attenuation and intensity attenuation have different exponents. A nonrelativistic barrier estimate outside its physical regime is only a formal textbook calculation.

methods.title: Explain tunneling confinement and resonance in a device
methods.principle: Finite barriers and energy matching determine leakage and transmission
steps: Identify the full potential including the outer regions
For an ideal infinite wall impose zero outside amplitude and hence zero transmitted current;do not infer finite leakage from a finite-width-barrier analogy
Distinguish truly bound levels from metastable levels between finite barriers
Compare single-barrier attenuation with double-barrier resonant transmission
Relate applied bias to level alignment
State how these changes affect current or confinement
methods.boundary: A finite well with exterior potential above the bound energy does not leak merely because its height is finite. Escape requires an energetically accessible outer region beyond a finite-width barrier.

methods.title: Bound a ground energy by minimizing an uncertainty-constrained energy
methods.principle: Position and momentum spreads cannot both be arbitrarily small
steps: Express kinetic and potential expectations in terms of means and variances
Choose the symmetry-compatible zero means for the ground-state bound
Use the position-momentum uncertainty lower bound
Eliminate one variance
Minimize the remaining positive energy function
Check whether a state exists that saturates all inequalities
methods.boundary: This minimization is distinct from merely inserting a confinement length into a kinetic-energy estimate. For a quadratic oscillator a Gaussian saturates the bound.

methods.title: Estimate confinement energy from uncertainty
methods.principle: Position-momentum uncertainty and kinetic energy
steps: Choose the stated confinement length as a position-width scale
Infer the minimal momentum-width scale
Estimate the associated kinetic energy
Convert that scale to the requested units or an energy-equivalent temperature
methods.boundary: Zero-point confinement energy is not a positive lower bound on thermodynamic temperature.

methods.title: Prove the overlap matrix of orthonormal bases is unitary
methods.principle: Resolution of identity and basis orthogonality
steps: Express transformation entries as basis overlaps
Multiply the matrix by its conjugate transpose
Sum over the complete intermediate basis
Reduce to orthonormal overlaps and the identity matrix

methods.title: Prove preservation of inner products under a unitary map
methods.principle: U-dagger U equals identity
steps: Transform both bra and ket
Reverse the transformed bra with the adjoint
Cancel the adjacent unitary inverse pair
Recover the original inner product or norm

methods.title: Constrain eigenvalues of a unitary operator
methods.principle: Norm preservation
steps: Apply the unitary operator to an eigenvector
Compare the transformed norm with the original norm
Replace the action by its eigenvalue
Infer unit modulus
methods.boundary: When the problem specifies a commuting Hermitian real/imaginary decomposition, obtain the same modulus condition from A-squared+B-squared=I in its common eigenbasis.

methods.title: Derive and apply the quantum virial relation
methods.principle: Mean evolution of the dilation observable
steps: Insert xp or its Hermitian symmetrization into the mean-motion identity
Evaluate the kinetic and potential commutators
Set the time derivative to zero in a stationary state
Relate kinetic energy to the potential derivative and specialize to its power law

methods.title: Estimate an exchange-interaction time and range from an energy scale
methods.principle: The inverse energy mismatch sets a characteristic time and Compton-like range
steps: Calculate the rest-energy mismatch for the stated hypothetical intermediate configuration
Form the order-of-magnitude time hbar divided by the energy scale
Multiply by the stipulated speed scale to estimate range
Compare observation duration with this timescale if requested
Explain the heuristic status of the construction
methods.boundary: Virtual exchange does not literally violate energy conservation or constitute an observable sequence of emitted and reabsorbed real particles. This estimate is not the lifetime-width formula for an actual unstable on-shell state.

methods.title: Estimate bound-state energies by a phase integral
methods.principle: Semiclassical action quantization
steps: Identify allowed intervals and local momentum
Classify each boundary as a hard wall or smooth turning point
Integrate the momentum over the interval with the appropriate boundary phases
Solve the quantization equation for energy
Check the semiclassical regime and expand in a small perturbation if requested
methods.boundary: Two hard walls do not have the half-integer phase offset of two soft turning points.

methods.title: Prove node ordering with increasing energy
methods.principle: Wronskian comparison at adjacent nodes
steps: Multiply/subtract the unequal-energy stationary equations
Integrate the Wronskian derivative between adjacent nodes
Assume the higher-energy state keeps one sign on the interval
Use endpoint slopes and integral signs to obtain a contradiction
methods.boundary: Shares the Wronskian construction with nondegeneracy, but adds a substantive nodal sign argument.

methods.title: Prove one-dimensional bound-state nondegeneracy
methods.principle: Wronskian of equal-energy solutions
steps: Multiply and subtract the two equal-energy stationary equations
Show their Wronskian is constant
Use decaying boundary values to set it to zero
Integrate the zero-Wronskian relation to establish proportionality

methods.title: Enumerate weak-field Zeeman spectral components
methods.principle: Magnetic energy shifts and transition rules
steps: Determine the magnetic factor and allowed m values at both levels
List transitions obeying the angular selection rules
Subtract the upper and lower magnetic shifts
Combine coincident frequencies and display the spectral pattern
methods.boundary: Deriving the magnetic factor from precession is separate when explicitly requested.

methods.title: Relate matter wavelength to particle motion
methods.principle: Matter wavelength is h divided by momentum magnitude
steps: Identify particle mass and whether supplied energy is kinetic or total
Obtain momentum from speed, kinetic energy or acceleration voltage
Use the relativistic relation when its corrections matter
Set lambda=h/p and invert for the requested motion if needed
Compare wavelength with an experimental length
State any missing mass or energy convention
methods.boundary: Changing momentum direction alone does not change wavelength magnitude. A zero-momentum eigenstate has infinite wavelength and is not spatially localized.

methods.title: Solve photoelectric thresholds and electron energy balance
methods.principle: Photon energy pays the work function before giving an electron kinetic energy
steps: Identify the stated electron-removal threshold: surface work function or explicitly supplied atomic shell binding energy
Convert incident frequency or wavelength to photon energy
Test the emission threshold before subtracting
Use the maximum kinetic energy to find stopping voltage or speed
Invert the balance for work function, cutoff or required radiation
Distinguish intensity effects from single-photon energy
For a shell-absorption filter,compare both photon energies with the tabulated edge and select an edge between them
methods.boundary: Below threshold there are no photoelectrons in the single-photon model, not electrons with negative kinetic energy. Explicit problem data override a different work function in another exercise. An atomic K-shell binding energy is not a metal surface work function;use the removal process the source explicitly specifies. Edge placement alone does not fix a practical filter thickness.

methods.title: Infer photoelectric parameters and model validity from measurements
methods.principle: Stopping voltage is linear in frequency while saturation current tracks flux
steps: Identify axes, sign conventions and controlled illumination variables
Read stopping voltage and saturation current from a current-voltage curve
With multiple frequencies extract the slope and intercept of stopping voltage versus frequency
Infer Planck constant and work function with the correct electron-charge factor
Compare lag, threshold and intensity observations with the single-photon model
State which parameters a single curve cannot determine independently
methods.boundary: Ordinary weak illumination supports the one-photon model; it does not prove multiphoton processes are impossible. Thermal broadening and thermionic current can alter measured curves.

methods.title: Relate photon counts to beam energy, power, heat or current
methods.principle: Total delivered energy equals photon number times individual photon energy
steps: Calculate individual photon energy
Convert incident intensity to power with illuminated area if required
Divide energy or power by photon energy for photon count or rate
Include stated absorption or quantum yield
Relate absorbed energy to the requested heat or emitted charge
Check that an assumed one-electron-per-photon yield is actually an idealization
methods.boundary: Without absorption efficiency and quantum yield, incident photon flux sets an ideal upper bound on a photoelectron rate. A maximum electron kinetic energy does not by itself specify the whole emitted energy distribution.

methods.title: Convert photon frequency, wavelength, energy and momentum
methods.principle: E=hf=hc/lambda and p=E/c for a vacuum photon
steps: Identify the supplied photon quantity and its units
Use the vacuum dispersion relation to obtain frequency or wavelength
Convert energy using Planck constant and momentum using E/c
If comparing a massive particle use its own energy-momentum relation
Distinguish one-photon properties from the number of photons
methods.boundary: A larger monochromatic beam intensity changes photon flux, not the energy or momentum of each photon.

methods.title: Estimate the temperature scale of photon recoil
methods.principle: Photon momentum gives an atom a recoil kinetic energy
steps: Compute photon momentum from wavelength
Compute recoil energy with the atomic mass
Compare with the specified thermal-energy convention
State the order-one convention and distinguish recoil from other cooling limits
methods.boundary: The recoil scale is not the Doppler temperature, which needs a transition linewidth.

methods.title: Explain experimental evidence for wave-particle behavior
methods.principle: Interference probabilities and localized energy transfer require complementary descriptions
steps: Identify the actual measured pattern or detection event
State the prediction of a purely classical particle or wave model
Compare it with interference, diffraction or photon-transfer evidence
Distinguish amplitude interference from single-event detection
State why reducing flux does not remove quantum interference
methods.boundary: Do not describe electron interference as collisions between different electrons; one-at-a-time experiments still build the pattern.

methods.title: Find the short-wavelength cutoff of an accelerated-particle X-ray source
methods.principle: A photon cannot carry more than the kinetic energy supplied to its charged projectile
steps: Calculate kinetic-energy gain from charge times accelerating voltage
Set the maximum photon energy equal to that gain under the heavy-target idealization
Convert to the minimum wavelength or invert for voltage
Compare changes of voltage or projectile mass at fixed charge
Check practical source and recoil assumptions
methods.boundary: The cutoff energy does not depend on projectile mass at fixed charge and voltage, though radiation yield does. Relativistic speed alone does not invalidate the work-energy relation qV.

methods.title: Evaluate a Planck spectral density and its equilibrium dependence
methods.principle: Universal equilibrium cavity spectrum as a function of temperature
steps: State the temperature and whether density is per frequency or wavelength
Use the corresponding Planck formula with consistent density units
Evaluate the specified point or form a same-temperature spectral ratio
For a conceptual cavity comparison use equilibrium universality rather than wall-material emissivity
methods.boundary: Deriving a spectral peak or integrating a band is listed separately. The universal cavity spectrum does not imply equal emission from arbitrary exposed nonblack surfaces.

methods.title: Integrate a thermal spectrum for total power or a band fraction
methods.principle: Planck spectral integral with its correct Jacobian
steps: Choose the spectral variable and actual integration bounds
Convert energy density to outgoing flux only with the stated angular distribution
Change to dimensionless photon energy,including the Jacobian
Evaluate the complete Bose integral or the requested finite-band integral
Normalize by the total when a fraction is wanted
Restore temperature scaling and physical constants
methods.boundary: Finite-band fractions can require numerical quadrature;isotropic cavity flux is c times energy density divided by four,not c times energy density.

methods.title: Derive or compare maxima of a Planck spectrum
methods.principle: Stationary point of the stated spectral density
steps: Specify density per frequency or per wavelength;they have different maxima
Introduce the dimensionless photon-energy over kT variable
Differentiate the complete density including its prefactor
Solve its nonzero extremum equation and check the maximum
Convert back to the requested frequency or wavelength
methods.boundary: Inverting the wavelength at one density maximum does not give the maximum of the other density.

methods.title: Relate thermal radiated power, temperature and emitting area
methods.principle: Integrated blackbody emission is proportional to area times temperature to the fourth
steps: Determine area and emissivity under the stated geometry
Express absolute temperatures in kelvins
Apply the Stefan law or its ratio form
Include incoming environmental radiation only if net exchange is requested
Solve the requested power, size or temperature comparison
methods.boundary: Total emitted power is not net cooling power; equal luminosity does not imply equal surface temperature when areas differ.

methods.title: Infer blackbody temperature or peak wavelength
methods.principle: The wavelength-density spectral peak varies inversely with absolute temperature
steps: Identify whether a thermal continuum is the assumed source
Convert temperature to kelvins
Apply the wavelength form of Wien displacement or take a ratio
Locate the peak in the electromagnetic spectrum
Distinguish the peak wavelength from the whole visible color
methods.boundary: A flame can have strong chemical emission lines, so color alone is not a universal thermometer. At high temperature a thermal source still emits visible light even when its peak is outside the visible band.

methods.title: Compose or reorient Lorentz boosts
methods.principle: Ordered Lorentz-matrix multiplication
steps: State whether each map changes axes or actively rotates vectors
Write the elementary rotation and boost matrices
Multiply in the order of successive transformations
Identify the resulting boost speed and any rotation
Check the transformed origin or invariant metric
methods.boundary: Non-collinear boosts do not in general commute; a spatial basis rotation alone is not a new boost.

methods.title: Classify causal vectors and construct their special frames
methods.principle: Minkowski norm and allowed subluminal boosts
steps: Evaluate or constrain the invariant norm
Use a spatial rotation to align the relevant vector when useful
Apply an admissible boost to remove its time or spatial component if possible
Track the time sign for future or past causal vectors
Use the resulting canonical form to prove ordering, orthogonality or existence of a rest frame
methods.boundary: Future and past are preserved by physical time-orientation-preserving boosts, not by a formal time-reversal transformation; the zero vector requires separate treatment.

methods.title: Calculate photon recoil in scattering by a material particle
methods.principle: Four-momentum conservation with a null photon and fixed electron mass
steps: Write incoming and outgoing photon four-momenta
Eliminate the final material-particle momentum
Square the conservation relation and cancel unchanged mass terms
Insert ray angles and initial material velocity
Solve the outgoing photon energy
Check recoil and limiting regimes

methods.title: Integrate relativistic motion under a constant three-force
methods.principle: Momentum grows linearly while velocity is nonlinear in momentum
steps: Integrate dp/dt=F with the specified initial momentum
Calculate E from the mass shell
Obtain velocity as p c squared/E
Integrate each position component
Eliminate time if requested
Check slow-motion and long-time limits
methods.boundary: A nonzero transverse initial momentum gives a different trajectory from the zero-momentum one-dimensional special case, using the same ordered calculation.

methods.title: Prove a scalar, vector or tensor transformation property
methods.principle: Substitution of the defining transformation rules
steps: Write the proposed relation in both frames
Substitute known vector, tensor and metric transformations
Preserve matrix order and contract the metric correctly
Cancel inverse or metric-preserving factors
Use arbitrariness of the test vector when required
Identify the required transformation or invariant
methods.boundary: Four-tensor transformations use both index factors; a Euclidean similarity formula cannot be inserted blindly.

methods.title: Calculate a relativistic photon frequency or wavelength shift
methods.principle: Lorentz transformation of the wave four-vector
steps: Identify source rest frequency and the observation-frame ray angle
Apply the corresponding Doppler factor
Convert frequency and wavelength inversely
Solve for speed or fractional shift as requested
Check approach, recession and transverse limits
methods.boundary: The angle must be defined in the frame of the chosen formula; transverse in one frame is not generally transverse in the other.

methods.title: Solve elastic two-body scattering through the CM frame
methods.principle: Conserved CM momentum magnitudes with a specified scattering angle
steps: Find the CM boost from total four-momentum
Transform the incident momenta
Preserve the individual CM energies and momentum magnitudes
Apply the stated reversal or scattering angle
Boost final momenta back
Recover velocities and angles in the requested frame
methods.boundary: Conservation alone permits the trivial unchanged branch; an actual specified head-on scattering selects momentum reversal.

methods.title: Infer speed, momentum or energy from relativistic mass-shell relations
methods.principle: E squared equals p squared c squared plus m squared c to the fourth
steps: Separate total, kinetic and rest energies
Use the mass-shell relation to find the missing magnitude
Use v=p c squared/E for speed
Convert units consistently
Check the nonrelativistic or massless boundary

methods.title: Transform spacetime events and compare their ordering
methods.principle: Lorentz transformation of event coordinates or separations
steps: Identify the same physical events in both frames
State the relative boost direction and sign
Write all known event positions and times
Apply the Lorentz transformation or its inverse
Enforce any same-position or simultaneous conditions
Compare the transformed coordinates and time ordering

methods.title: Find electric and magnetic fields in a moving frame
methods.principle: Lorentz transformation of electromagnetic fields
steps: Choose a frame in which the source fields are known simply
Resolve fields parallel and perpendicular to the boost
Transform both electric and magnetic components with the correct sign
Transform source density and event coordinates where needed
Reexpress the result in the observation frame
Check a limiting orientation or speed

methods.title: Prove and use electromagnetic field invariants
methods.principle: E dot B and E squared minus c squared B squared
steps: Substitute the field boost component formulas
Expand the proposed scalar combinations
Cancel mixed terms using gamma squared times one minus beta squared
Extend from a standard boost to rotations and general boosts
Infer whether orthogonality or a field-free frame is possible

methods.title: Transform three-force between inertial frames
methods.principle: Four-force transformation or transformed momentum differential
steps: Form the four-force or momentum differentials
Apply the Lorentz boost
Transform the coordinate-time denominator
Divide to recover three-force components
Substitute the particle velocity and compare longitudinal and transverse factors

methods.title: Relate force, acceleration, power and changing rest mass
methods.principle: Differentiate relativistic momentum and its mass shell
steps: State whether rest mass is fixed
Differentiate p=gamma m v or p dot p=-m squared c squared
Use proper-time and coordinate-time conversion consistently
Contract with velocity when useful
Solve for the requested acceleration, power or mass-change identity

methods.title: Evaluate a Lorentz scalar in a convenient rest frame
methods.principle: Scalar products are frame independent
steps: Identify the invariant contraction and metric convention
Choose the rest frame of one timelike vector when useful
Insert the simple components there
Evaluate the contraction
Express the answer in invariant masses, proper quantities or relative gamma
Conclude the identity in every frame

methods.title: Compare simultaneous lengths and orientations between frames
methods.principle: Only the component parallel to the boost contracts
steps: Identify the proper shape and the direction of the boost
Resolve endpoint separation into parallel and transverse components
Contract the parallel component by gamma while retaining transverse components
Recombine to find length and angle
Impose simultaneity in the measuring frame
methods.boundary: This is a simultaneous-coordinate length, not the retarded optical image.

methods.title: Convert a reaction energy release into a rest-mass defect
methods.principle: Conservation of total energy including rest energy
steps: List the initial and final rest masses or internal energies
Calculate their difference with consistent particle counts
Multiply or divide by c squared
Scale the event count if a macroscopic sample is specified
Distinguish the change in sum of rest masses from the invariant mass of the complete isolated system

methods.title: Compare elapsed clock times along a relativistic trip
methods.principle: Proper time is the integral of dt divided by gamma
steps: Identify the clock worldline and the frame of each stated time
Compute gamma for each constant-speed leg
Convert coordinate time to proper time or solve the inverse relation
Sum successive legs when the clock changes inertial frames
Compare elapsed times without assuming the return trip uses a single comoving inertial frame

methods.title: Relate observed light-arrival intervals or apparent lengths to moving sources
methods.principle: Arrival time equals emission time plus propagation time
steps: Specify source worldlines and observer position
Write the light-travel distance for each emission event
Impose a common arrival time or subtract successive arrival times
Combine with clock dilation or simultaneous geometric length
Interpret approach and recession separately
methods.boundary: Apparent length and observed tick-arrival rate are not the same as frame-measured length and clock rate.

methods.title: Find composite invariant mass and center-of-momentum velocity
methods.principle: Sum four-momenta before taking the invariant norm
steps: Compute each constituent energy and momentum in one frame
Sum energy and vector momentum
Evaluate invariant mass from total E and total p
Use total p c squared/total E for the composite or CM velocity
Interpret why rest masses are not simply additive when relative motion is present

methods.title: Translate between covariant electromagnetic equations and components
methods.principle: Metric contractions and antisymmetric field-tensor entries
steps: State metric signature and component ordering
Insert the definitions of field tensor, four-potential or four-current
Expand the contraction or antisymmetric derivative component by component
Recognize the corresponding vector gradient, curl or divergence
Check signs and factors of c
Reassemble the compact equation
methods.boundary: This verifies equivalence of formulations; it is not a boundary-value solution of Maxwell equations.

methods.title: Find or rule out a relativistic reaction threshold
methods.principle: Invariant total four-momentum and minimum final rest energy
steps: Sum the initial four-momenta
Compute invariant collision energy
Set the minimum CM energy equal to the sum of allowed final rest energies
Solve for incident total or kinetic energy in the stated frame
Check whether a zero-mass initial invariant forbids the process
State any heavy-target approximation

methods.title: Solve two-body decay using four-momentum conservation
methods.principle: Parent rest-frame momentum balance and daughter mass shells
steps: Choose the parent rest frame
Set daughter momenta equal and opposite
Use total energy and both mass-shell relations to determine energies and momentum
Check the mass threshold
Transform the daughter momenta or velocities if another frame is requested
methods.boundary: Covers equal or unequal masses and a massless daughter; no independent new type arises from naming a different particle.

methods.title: Transform particle velocity between inertial frames
methods.principle: Relativistic parallel and transverse velocity transformation
steps: Distinguish particle velocity from relative frame velocity
Resolve parallel and transverse components
Transform the four-velocity components and divide spatial components by the time component to derive, or directly apply, the common-denominator three-velocity formula
Recombine components for speed and direction
Check subluminal or lightlike limits
methods.boundary: Closing speed measured in a third frame is not either particle rest-frame relative speed.

methods.title: Prove a four-vector vanishes from an all-frame zero component
methods.principle: Boosts mix time and spatial components
steps: Write a boost along a chosen axis
Apply the assumed zero component in both frames
Vary the boost to force its mixed partner to vanish
Rotate or repeat along the other axes
Conclude the full vector is zero

methods.title: Assess what an experiment can establish about a physical model
methods.principle: A reproducible contradiction can reject a specified prediction, while agreement has limited scope
steps: State the model prediction and its assumptions
Identify the observed comparison and uncertainty
Distinguish a failed prediction from faulty auxiliary assumptions or measurement
Explain why a finite set of successful tests is not a universal logical proof
methods.boundary: Not every noisy discrepant datum alone refutes a theory.

methods.title: Compare structural flexibility and load support from construction
methods.principle: Material identity alone does not determine the response of a structure
steps: Identify whether the applied loading is tensile, compressive or bending
Identify the connected load-bearing sections and whether parts can slide or rearrange
Compare axial support with resistance to curvature or buckling
State which construction is useful for each loading mode and distinguish material modulus from structural stiffness
methods.boundary: Equal outside diameter need not mean equal load-bearing material area. This qualitative comparison is not a numerical Euler-buckling or beam-deflection derivation.

methods.title: Relate load and small deformation using the appropriate elastic modulus
methods.principle: Stress equals the mode-specific modulus times strain
steps: Identify axial stretch/compression, volumetric compression or shear
Calculate the correct normal/tangential force per loaded area, or pressure change
Define strain as length change/original length, negative volume change/original volume, or transverse displacement/face separation
Use Young, bulk or shear modulus for that mode and solve for the unknown
For serial regions use the actual internal load and add the local deformations
Check unit conversions and the small-strain elastic approximation
methods.boundary: These algebraic steps are shared across the three modes, but their stress/strain definitions must be labeled. Breaking stress is not Young modulus. Mixed loading can require separate force-balance and geometric compatibility calculations.
