methods.principle: Combine gas transport with dilute and condensed molar volumes
steps: Infer mean free path from measured conductivity and macroscopic heat capacity and speed
Express gas path length using molecular cross section and unknown particle number
Estimate molecular volume from condensed-phase density and molar volume
Eliminate the molecular size to recover particle number per mole
Keep the geometric and kinetic factors explicitly approximate
methods.boundary: Do not insert a known Boltzmann constant, molecular mass, molecular diameter or Avogadro number into a problem asking to infer that number.

methods.title: Derive a transport coefficient from molecular exchange across a plane
methods.principle: Particles carry locally sampled energy, momentum or concentration across a mean free path
steps: Choose equal crossing populations on the two sides
Express the transported content difference by the local gradient
Multiply by crossing rate and mean free path
Match to the macroscopic constitutive law
Substitute density, thermal speed and collision-length scalings
Evaluate and explain pressure and temperature dependence
methods.boundary: The transported quantity determines the storage factor. Viscosity and conductivity lose the density factor, but particle diffusivity does not.

methods.title: Estimate collision distance or infer density from it
methods.principle: One collision per swept interaction volume on average
steps: Specify effective collision cross section
Multiply by target number density for inverse path length
Insert the equation of state to relate number density and pressure
Solve for the requested path, pressure or time
State the order-one kinetic correction and molecular-size model

methods.title: Reduce a variational path using an absent independent variable
methods.principle: Beltrami first integral
steps: Verify that the integrand has no explicit independent-variable dependence
Form integrand minus slope times its slope derivative
Set this expression equal to a constant
Solve the first-order equation for the slope
Integrate and fit the boundary or length conditions
Check admissible branches
methods.boundary: This conservation identity is different from the cyclic-dependent-coordinate identity, though a variable exchange can relate routes for a particular problem.

methods.title: Derive the Beltrami conservation identity
methods.principle: Chain rule and Euler-Lagrange equation
steps: Differentiate the integrand along the stationary curve
Expand through its dependent coordinate and derivative
Replace the coordinate partial derivative by the Euler-Lagrange expression
Recognize a total product derivative
Conclude that integrand minus slope times its conjugate derivative is constant

methods.title: Reduce a variational path using an absent dependent coordinate
methods.principle: Conserved derivative of the integrand with respect to path slope
steps: Identify the coordinate absent from the integrand
Set the derivative with respect to its slope equal to a constant
Solve for the slope
Integrate on the permitted coordinate branches
Fit endpoints and describe the geometric curve
Compare branches or winding classes when shortestness is requested

methods.title: Find a stationary path from an explicit variational integrand
methods.principle: Euler-Lagrange differential equation
steps: Write the functional with a clearly identified dependent variable and derivative
Evaluate its two partial derivatives
Form the Euler-Lagrange differential equation
Solve it or verify the proposed solution family
Impose the endpoint conditions
Distinguish stationarity from a proved minimum

methods.title: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from independent variations
methods.principle: Stationarity and integration by parts
steps: Perturb each dependent coordinate independently with an endpoint-vanishing test function
Differentiate the functional with respect to each perturbation parameter
Integrate derivative-variation terms by parts
Remove the fixed-endpoint boundary terms
Use arbitrary independent variations to set each remaining coefficient to zero

methods.title: Prove invariance under adding a total time derivative to L
methods.principle: Fixed-endpoint action differs only by an endpoint term
steps: Express the added term as d f(q,t)/dt
Integrate it to an endpoint difference or expand its Euler-Lagrange derivatives
Show the endpoint variation vanishes or partial-derivative terms cancel
Conclude identical equations of motion

methods.title: Derive or evaluate area from a vector cross product
methods.principle: Triangle base times height
steps: Choose the two edge vectors from a shared vertex
Relate their perpendicular projection to the included-angle sine
Evaluate the cross-product magnitude
Take half for a triangle
Preserve orientation only when an oriented area is requested
For a closed planar curve,triangulate it into infinitesimal oriented areas and integrate their one-half position-cross-displacement contribution

methods.title: Construct and invert curvilinear unit-vector relations
methods.principle: Orthonormal bases tangent to coordinate lines
steps: Write the Cartesian position map
Differentiate along each coordinate and normalize or use geometric projections
Express the moving basis in Cartesian components
Invert by transposing the orthonormal coefficient matrix
Verify dot products and handedness
When time dependence is requested,differentiate the angle-dependent components and regroup in the moving basis
methods.boundary: This is basis construction, not solving a trajectory in those coordinates.

methods.title: Rewrite a vector field in a different or coordinate-free basis
methods.principle: Projection on local orthonormal unit vectors
steps: Express each local unit vector in the common basis
Project fixed vectors onto the local directions
Substitute into the supplied vector expression
Combine terms using scalar products
Check a simple axial or transverse direction
methods.boundary: Coordinate-dependent unit vectors must not be treated as constants during differentiation or angular integration.

methods.title: Resolve,combine and normalize geometric vectors
methods.principle: Cartesian vector components and Euclidean norm
steps: Express directed segments or given vectors in a common basis
Add the specified signed components or subtract endpoints
Use norms and the coordinate geometry to find lengths or direction angles
Normalize to obtain a unit direction when requested
Check quadrants,zero-vector exceptions and the distinction between path length and displacement

methods.title: Evaluate an oriented cross product or reconstruct a vector constrained by it
methods.principle: Antisymmetric component products and the right-hand orientation
steps: Express the ordered input vectors in the same right-handed orthonormal basis
Evaluate all three antisymmetric component differences
Retain factor order and any signed charge or scalar multiplier
Calculate the norm or normalize the result if requested
If the product is prescribed,solve its component equations and retain any unconstrained parallel component
Check perpendicularity and the direction by a simple limiting orientation
methods.boundary: Torque uses position from the stated pivot cross force; particle angular momentum uses position cross momentum. These are the same component procedure,not separate types named after the resulting physical quantity.

methods.title: Calculate curl and test local conservativity
methods.principle: Antisymmetrized derivatives of vector components
steps: Express the field in the requested coordinate basis
Apply the corresponding Cartesian or curvilinear curl operator including scale factors
Differentiate and simplify every component
Identify singular or excluded points
Interpret a zero curl with the required domain assumptions
methods.boundary: A locally zero curl alone does not prove path independence in a domain with topological obstructions. Explicit requests for both coordinate routes are retained.

methods.title: Prove a vector product or norm relation from geometry
methods.principle: Equivalence of Cartesian components and Euclidean projections
steps: Choose axes aligned with the relevant vector or plane
Write the components and lengths by projection or Pythagoras
Evaluate the component expression
Equate it with the geometric magnitude and orientation
Track signs and any zero-vector exception
For a volume formula,use the oriented base area and perpendicular height before taking the absolute value
methods.boundary: Component algebra alone does not fulfill a requested geometric proof. Dot, cross and norm cases retain their specified geometric outputs.

methods.title: Apply a vector-weighted directional derivative
methods.principle: The differential operator acts on the following field
steps: Expand A dot del in coordinates
Apply it to each component of the target
Include derivatives of moving basis vectors when present
Reassemble the resulting vector
Exclude coordinate singularities or take regular limits

methods.title: Calculate divergence and interpret local expansion
methods.principle: Coordinate expression for divergence
steps: Choose the correct coordinate formula
Differentiate the matching components including metric factors
Sum the terms
Identify singular points excluded from ordinary differentiation
Relate the sign to local net outward flow

methods.title: Replace closed-surface flux by a volume divergence integral
methods.principle: Divergence theorem on a regular domain
steps: Specify the closed surface and enclosed volume
Check smoothness or isolate singularities
Evaluate divergence
Integrate it over the volume with the appropriate measure
Match the result to outward surface flux

methods.title: Prove the divergence theorem for a rectangular box
methods.principle: Fundamental theorem of calculus on pairs of faces
steps: Pair opposite faces with their signed normals
Write each pair as a difference of field components
Express the difference as an integral of its coordinate derivative
Combine with the transverse integrals
Sum the three coordinate contributions into the volume integral of divergence

methods.title: Evaluate a dot product,projection or included angle from components
methods.principle: Scalar product is the sum of corresponding component products
steps: Express both vectors in one orthonormal basis
Multiply corresponding components and sum
Calculate the operand norms when an angle or normalized projection is requested
Solve the cosine relation or the stated linear dot-product constraint
Retain signs,all permitted angles and zero-vector exceptions
methods.boundary: A cross product uses a different component operation. A conceptual comparison of both products is separately listed.

methods.title: Construct a field satisfying specified zero divergence and curl
methods.principle: A harmonic scalar has a divergence-free gradient
steps: Choose a nonconstant harmonic polynomial or an equivalent component ansatz
Form its gradient
Calculate divergence and curl explicitly
Verify the claimed domain and smoothness
methods.boundary: A constant field is excluded when the question asks for a nontrivial example.

methods.title: Prove dot or cross distributivity from geometry
methods.principle: Signed projections and oriented parallelogram areas
steps: Draw the vector sum
Resolve projections parallel and perpendicular to the fixed vector
Add signed projections or oriented areas
Recombine perpendicular components in the noncoplanar case
methods.boundary: The source explicitly requests geometric definitions and diagrams, not only a component expansion.

methods.title: Differentiate a scalar field or obtain its force
methods.principle: Coordinate partial derivatives and the chain rule
steps: Hold the other coordinates fixed in each partial derivative
Differentiate all explicit and implicit coordinate dependencies
Assemble the gradient components
Negate for force when requested
Evaluate the specified point or parameter values

methods.title: Find normals and the steepest change of a scalar field
methods.principle: Directional derivative and level-set constraint
steps: Identify the level surface
Set the first-order change to zero along its tangent
Infer that the gradient is normal
Normalize the gradient for a unit normal or steepest-ascent direction
Maximize the gradient-displacement dot product at fixed displacement length

methods.title: Predict a small field change from its gradient
methods.principle: First-order multivariable differential
steps: Calculate the gradient at the initial point
Form its dot product with the specified displacement
Evaluate the exact finite change when requested
Compare the neglected higher-order terms

methods.title: Check a gradient line integral against endpoint values
methods.principle: Integral of an exact differential
steps: Differentiate the supplied scalar
Parameterize each requested path with its orientation
Integrate gradient dot displacement
Independently evaluate the endpoint difference
Compare all requested paths
methods.boundary: Checking the theorem requires the requested explicit path calculation as well as an endpoint subtraction.

methods.title: Derive vector integration-by-parts and integral identities
methods.principle: Product rules plus the divergence or Stokes theorem
steps: Choose the product field that generates the desired integrand
Expand its derivative
Integrate over the specified region
Convert the total derivative to its oriented boundary integral
Rearrange and retain all boundary terms
Use an arbitrary constant test vector to recover a vector identity when necessary

methods.title: Evaluate the scalar or Cartesian-component vector Laplacian
methods.principle: Divergence of gradient with coordinate metric factors
steps: Select the correct scalar Laplacian
Substitute the scalar or each Cartesian component
Differentiate including all coordinate factors
Simplify and specify excluded singular points
Transform to Cartesian coordinates for an independent check when requested
methods.boundary: A vector Laplacian is not obtained by applying the scalar formula independently to moving-basis components.

methods.title: Evaluate an oriented line integral or variable-force work
methods.principle: Parameterized vector line integral
steps: Parameterize each oriented segment
Substitute its coordinates into the vector field
Differentiate the path to obtain its tangent element
Integrate the specified field-tangent dot or cross product componentwise over the parameter range;work uses the dot product
Add segments and compare specified paths
For rigid rotation use the equivalent angular work integral of torque times angular displacement,or torque times angular velocity integrated over time
methods.boundary: For a one-dimensional force graph, the integral can be evaluated by signed geometric areas. A force that always follows the path requires integration along arclength; substituting a straight chord is incorrect. Reversing oriented limits changes sign only for a fixed position field, not for kinetic friction that reverses with motion.

methods.title: Bound a vector norm using dot-product geometry
methods.principle: Cauchy-Schwarz and nonnegative squared norms
steps: Expand the relevant squared norm or cross-product magnitude
Bound the dot or cross product by the product of norms
Retain equality and orientation conditions
Take a nonnegative square root or divide only by a positive scale
methods.boundary: An inequality over an entire trajectory may also require a separate scalar monotonicity test.

methods.title: Classify vector and scalar products under translation or inversion
methods.principle: Transform every factor and retain cross-product orientation
steps: Distinguish a fixed vector from a newly chosen position vector
Transform polar components
Apply the transformation to every factor of a product
Track axial-vector and pseudoscalar signs
Give physical examples with the same transformation law

methods.title: Prove or disprove path independence by comparing paths
methods.principle: Work differences and closed loops
steps: Construct two paths with the same endpoints or a forward and reversed path
Express their work difference as a closed-loop integral
Use the stipulated path-independent work or central-force geometry
Vary endpoints or infinitesimal radial segments to establish the required condition
State the accessible domain

methods.title: Infer vector geometry from dot and cross products
methods.principle: Dot products measure parallel projection and cross products oriented perpendicular area
steps: Check whether each operand and output is a scalar or vector
Express the products using norms, sine or cosine and orientation
Apply zero, extremal or specified-product constraints
Retain all allowed angles, orientations and zero-vector exceptions
Use geometric perpendicularity for an explicitly requested geometric proof
methods.boundary: Applying product geometry is not a full derivation of a triple-product identity or a differential vector-calculus theorem.

methods.title: Prove a vector product differentiation rule
methods.principle: Componentwise scalar product rules
steps: Expand the scalar or vector product in components
Differentiate each scalar product
Regroup terms into the requested vector expression
Preserve factor order for a cross product

methods.title: Distinguish scalars,vectors and their required specifications
methods.principle: A spatial vector has magnitude,direction and the appropriate coordinate transformation
steps: Identify what physical information the proposed quantity supplies
Test whether spatial components and direction are required and how they transform
Distinguish a sign or temporal ordering from a spatial direction
Identify any missing magnitude or direction needed to specify the quantity
methods.boundary: Calling time a temporal arrow does not make it a three-dimensional spatial vector. A scalar field assigns scalars at positions; its spatial dependence alone does not make it a vector field.

methods.title: Add or close displacement vectors with a scale drawing
methods.principle: Head-to-tail vector addition preserves magnitude and direction
steps: Choose a consistent length scale and reference direction
Draw each directed segment head to tail, reversing any subtracted vector
Join the starting and ending points or close the polygon
Measure the resultant length and angle
Convert the plotted length back into physical units and assess graphical precision
methods.boundary: Keep this explicitly requested graphical route even when a component calculation is also requested; it is not another physical law.

methods.title: Relate zero divergence to flux and surface independence
methods.principle: Divergence theorem and cancellation of shared boundaries
steps: Apply divergence of curl when a potential is supplied
Convert closed flux to the volume divergence
Join two equally bounded surfaces with opposite orientations
Cancel common pieces
Use arbitrarily small volumes for the converse
methods.boundary: Assume the field is regular on the enclosed volumes; topology and singularities cannot be ignored.

methods.title: Evaluate and compare circulation and surface curl flux
methods.principle: Stokes theorem with consistent orientation
steps: Identify the oriented loop and a spanning surface
Calculate the curl and the oriented area element
Integrate curl flux
Independently parameterize and integrate the boundary when a check is requested
Compare the two results
methods.boundary: Keep distinct from deriving the theorem; irregular fields require a domain check.

methods.title: Connect circulation and curl through Stokes theorem
methods.principle: Boundary orientation and the fundamental theorem of calculus
steps: Write the oriented boundary integral
For a rectangle group opposite edges
Use one-dimensional integral differences to obtain the surface curl
Extend or invoke the oriented-surface theorem as requested
Infer the zero-circulation criterion with an admissible spanning surface

methods.title: Calculate or interpret oriented flux through a surface
methods.principle: Normal component times oriented area
steps: Parameterize the requested surface or its faces
Choose the outward or specified normal
Evaluate the vector field on that surface
Form the signed normal component times area
Integrate when requested
Interpret inward and outward contributions separately

methods.title: Expand vector products and prove algebraic vector identities
methods.principle: Cartesian cross-product components or Levi-Civita contraction
steps: Write the vector products in components
Contract the repeated indices or expand the determinant
Collect dot products and scalar factors
Compare each component with the claimed identity
Retain the order and sign of each cross product
If products are prescribed as constraints,rearrange the identity to reconstruct the unknown vector and verify both constraints

methods.title: Construct a vector potential for a solenoidal field
methods.principle: Field equals curl of a potential
steps: Check divergence and domain conditions
Choose a simple component or gauge ansatz
Integrate the curl component equations
Fix remaining functions by the other components
Verify the full curl and explain gradient gauge freedom
methods.boundary: Existence is domain dependent; a local zero-divergence test alone does not prove a global potential on every punctured domain.

methods.title: Relate acoustic displacement, pressure amplitude and intensity
methods.principle: Linear compression and traveling-wave impedance connect the amplitudes
steps: Use p=-B*partial y/partial x to relate pressure and displacement for the wave
For a sinusoidal progressive wave apply pmax=B*k*A=rho*v*omega*A
Apply I=pmax squared/(2*rho*v)=rho*v*omega squared*A squared/2
Solve for the requested amplitude, intensity or frequency and preserve unit prefixes
Explain amplitude ratios at fixed medium properties
methods.boundary: This is peak rather than rms pressure. A nonsinusoidal profile requires its actual derivatives or integrals. Sound-pressure level in a coherent opposing-wave field must not be confused with net directed acoustic energy flux.

methods.title: Recover displacement and particle motion from a nonsinusoidal pressure wave
methods.principle: Pressure is minus bulk modulus times the displacement gradient
steps: Read the piecewise pressure profile and its spatial period
Integrate -p/B to obtain displacement, fixing the stated integration constant
Propagate the profile with x-v*t and distinguish spatial and temporal plots
Differentiate displacement to get particle velocity and acceleration on each smooth segment
State one-sided behavior or jumps at idealized corners
Draw every requested cycle and explain the corresponding source motion
methods.boundary: Do not substitute sinusoidal amplitude formulas for a triangular or rectangular pressure waveform. Ideal corners may give discontinuous acceleration rather than an infinite velocity.

methods.title: Infer nearby frequencies from beats and tuning changes
methods.principle: Beat frequency equals the absolute frequency difference
steps: Obtain each frequency in the listener frame
Use fbeat=abs(f1-f2)
Retain both above and below branches until a tuning-direction observation resolves them
Track how changing length, tension or motion changes the beat rate
Distinguish slow audible intensity modulation from rapidly unresolved roughness
methods.boundary: The envelope cosine has half the frequency difference, but its absolute-magnitude peaks occur at the full difference. Doppler-shifting a component or finding its resonator frequency is an added step.

methods.title: Calculate classical Doppler shifts with a material medium
methods.principle: Source motion sets crest spacing and listener motion sets the crest encounter rate
steps: Choose the propagation direction and express source and receiver velocities relative to the medium
Use lambda=(v-u_source_along_ray)/f_source
Use f_received=(v-u_receiver_along_ray)/lambda
For an echo first calculate the target received frequency, then treat that target as a moving source on the return ray
Solve the requested speed or frequency and check approach or recession signs
For changing geometry use the source velocity projection at emission and account for travel delay when relevant
methods.boundary: Source and receiver motion are not interchangeable even at equal relative speeds. Wavelength does not change under a Galilean receiver-frame change; the wave speed relative to that receiver does. A uniform wind changes both medium-frame velocities. Light instead requires the relativistic Doppler method.

methods.title: Find two-path interference phases,fringes and intensities
methods.principle: Coherent amplitude addition with phase set by path difference
steps: Compute both path lengths or their justified far-field difference
Convert path difference to phase and include the source phase offset
Solve integer or half-integer wavelength conditions within the geometric domain
Convert angles to screen positions without assuming a small angle unless justified
For signal strength add complex amplitudes or the equivalent cosine interference term
Include unequal amplitudes and any separately specified diffraction envelope
methods.boundary: Opposite phase gives complete cancellation only for equal received amplitudes. Rapidly varying amplitudes can shift extrema of total intensity away from pure phase-opposition points.

methods.title: Obtain attenuation and phase from a damped wave equation
methods.principle: Complex wave number from a harmonic ansatz
steps: Derive or take the wave PDE including its first-time-derivative loss term
Insert a harmonic temporal dependence with an explicit sign convention
Solve the complex dispersion relation
Choose the spatially decaying outgoing branch
Extract wavelength, phase speed, penetration depth and relative field phase
Check good-loss and weak-loss limits
methods.boundary: Field amplitude penetration length is one over the imaginary wave number; intensity decays twice as fast. Opposite time conventions change complex signs, not physical damping.

methods.title: Convert logarithmic sound levels and intensity ratios
methods.principle: Level difference is ten times the base-ten logarithm of the intensity ratio
steps: Use beta=10*log10(I/I0) with I0=1e-12 W/m squared when the source specifies the standard reference
Invert the logarithm or subtract levels to find intensity ratios
For independent incoherent sources add intensities before taking the logarithm
For a given decibel attenuation per distance and frequency accumulate the specified path loss
Distinguish a negative level from a negative physical intensity and a decibel difference from a level ratio
methods.boundary: Never add decibel levels arithmetically for independent sources. Coherent sources require phase-aware amplitudes before conversion. These textbook levels do not certify safe exposure. A specified voltage-amplitude transfer uses20 log10(amplitude ratio), equivalent to10log10(power ratio) only for equal reference impedances.

methods.title: Explain shallow-water wave steepening from depth-dependent speed
methods.principle: Different portions of a surface-wave profile travel at different depth-dependent speeds
steps: Use the supplied increase of wave speed with local water depth
Compare the propagation of the deeper crest region with the shallower leading portion
Track the resulting forward steepening as the wave reaches shallow water
Identify overturning or breaking as failure of the small-amplitude profile model
methods.boundary: This is the qualitative depth-speed mechanism requested by the source,not a quantitative breaking-height law or merely a transverse/longitudinal classification.

methods.title: Find phase and group speeds from a dispersion relation
methods.principle: Phase omega/k and group derivative d omega/d k
steps: Express omega as a function of k or k as a function of omega
Differentiate using the actual model parameters
Evaluate phase and group velocities separately
Analyze limiting behavior or resonance singularities
Plot the requested parameter domain when required
Interpret packet, energy and causal-signal speed distinctly
methods.boundary: A superluminal formal phase or group velocity near absorption is not automatically superluminal signal propagation.

methods.title: Construct an electromagnetic plane wave from direction and polarization
methods.principle: Transversality and B equals wave-vector cross E over frequency
steps: Normalize the propagation vector and set its magnitude from dispersion
Choose a unit electric polarization perpendicular to propagation
Obtain magnetic polarization and amplitude by the cross-product relation
Write real spatial and temporal phases
Check E cross B points along propagation
Preserve the sign or phase freedom in the chosen polarization basis

methods.title: Find allowed conducting-guide or cavity modes
methods.principle: Transverse Helmholtz eigenfunctions and conductor boundary conditions
steps: Choose TE or TM longitudinal field relative to the guide axis
Separate the transverse Helmholtz equation
Impose the corresponding Neumann or Dirichlet wall conditions
Reject index combinations whose entire field is zero
Recover every transverse field from Maxwell equations
Infer cutoff and dispersion and impose end-wall standing waves for a closed cavity
methods.boundary: TE and TM have different zero-index restrictions. A single-conductor hollow guide has no nonzero TEM mode; a coaxial two-conductor line can support one.

methods.title: Reduce Maxwell equations to longitudinal guide fields
methods.principle: Harmonic guide ansatz and vector differential constraints
steps: Insert the common longitudinal and temporal exponential into all Maxwell equations
Expand their components in the transverse coordinates
Solve the coupled equations for transverse fields from longitudinal ones
Derive the transverse Helmholtz equations by substitution
Check both divergence and remaining curl constraints
Handle the zero denominator TEM case directly rather than dividing by zero

methods.title: Recover traveling-wave amplitudes from initial displacement and velocity
methods.principle: Fourier inversion with two independent initial data
steps: Express the real wave as a modal integral with its temporal convention
Evaluate both displacement and time derivative at the initial time
Fourier transform both functions
Solve for the positive/negative direction coefficients while imposing the real-field conjugacy relation
Recover the specified complex-amplitude convention
Treat the zero-frequency component separately if present
methods.boundary: Initial displacement alone does not determine both traveling directions; do not omit the velocity transform or its omega factor.

methods.title: Find coherent reflection and transmission by interface matching
methods.principle: Traveling-wave amplitudes constrained at every material interface
steps: Write incident and outgoing waves in exterior regions and both directions in every finite internal layer
Keep common frequency and conserved tangential wave number
Choose the physical displacement/force or electromagnetic boundary conditions
Include the propagation phase between distinct interfaces
Solve the complete linear amplitude system or its equivalent coherent multiple-reflection sum
Convert amplitudes to flux ratios with impedances and projected areas
Check zero-thickness,single-interface and lossless-conservation limits
methods.boundary: A massive string knot modifies force balance;permeability modifies optical impedance. Complex wave numbers describe loss. Time-domain pulse profiles additionally require functional matching and width rescaling.

methods.title: Analyze a supersonic Mach cone and arrival of its shock front
methods.principle: The envelope of emitted wavefronts has sin(cone half-angle)=sound speed/source speed
steps: Identify the source trajectory and sound speed relative to the medium
Use Mach number and the cone half-angle relation
Locate observers ahead of, on or inside the trailing cone
Use the altitude and cone geometry to find the source position when the front arrives
Convert source travel distance to the time since closest passage
Distinguish crossing the shock front from sound heard within the cone
methods.boundary: A boom is not emitted only once when Mach 1 is crossed. A co-moving occupant does not repeatedly cross the aircraft own shock front.

methods.title: Identify particle motion and restoring mechanisms in a mechanical wave
methods.principle: Longitudinal or transverse classification compares displacement with propagation
steps: Identify the direction of propagation separately from particle displacement
Resolve displacement into parallel and perpendicular components
Identify the elastic or other restoring force that can support the proposed deformation
Explain energy transport without requiring net transport of medium material
State whether the simple linear model can represent the proposed effect
methods.boundary: Surface waves can mix longitudinal and transverse motion. Breaking waves require more than a small-amplitude linear traveling sine wave.

methods.title: Derive a mechanical wave equation from local force balance
methods.principle: Newton balance on an infinitesimal elastic medium element
steps: Choose the element and its mass per length,area or volume
Resolve the elastic forces on its opposing faces using the small-displacement constitutive relation
Include a specified local drag force before taking the continuum limit
Divide by element size and obtain the spatial and temporal derivatives
Identify the wave-speed and any damping coefficients and their units
methods.boundary: Deriving the governing equation is distinct from differentiating a proposed function to check an already supplied equation.

methods.title: Calculate and interpret mechanical-wave energy transfer
methods.principle: Transverse tension work transports kinetic and elastic energy
steps: Identify the local transverse force component and transverse particle velocity
Use P=-F*(partial y/partial x)*(partial y/partial t) when instantaneous work or a derivation is required
For a sinusoidal traveling string wave use average P=mu*v*omega squared*A squared/2 and peak P twice its average
Apply the requested amplitude, frequency, tension or speed changes while identifying fixed parameters
Integrate over time when total energy is asked and distinguish dissipation from geometric spreading
methods.boundary: For a standing wave the two directions have equal and opposite mean flux; at a node transverse velocity and transmitted power vanish. Source power is not the algebraic mean displacement.

methods.title: Construct wave solutions by separation and mode superposition
methods.principle: Separated spatial and temporal eigenfunctions
steps: Insert a product of spatial and temporal factors into the PDE
Separate with consistent eigenvalue signs
Solve the independent ordinary equations
Impose boundary and regularity conditions
Superpose admissible modes or continuous wave numbers
Relate mode coefficients to the supplied data
methods.boundary: A scalar wave-equation solution need not satisfy the additional vector constraints of Maxwell equations.

methods.title: Select propagating modes from cutoff inequalities
methods.principle: Driving frequency exceeds an allowed modal cutoff
steps: List the permitted mode-index combinations
Calculate each cutoff with the actual guide dimensions
Retain those below the driving frequency
Identify the lowest and next distinct cutoff for single-mode operation
Convert between angular frequency, frequency and free-space wavelength
Handle cutoff equality and degeneracy explicitly
methods.boundary: TM indices cannot be copied from TE; frequencies quoted in hertz require the two-pi conversion.

methods.title: Transform a wave frequency to a moving nonrelativistic frame
methods.principle: Invariant wave phase under a Galilean coordinate change
steps: Substitute the moving-frame coordinate into the phase
Identify the coefficient of time and the unchanged wavevector
Multiply by hbar when an excitation energy is requested
State the nonrelativistic or first-order-in-speed approximation
methods.boundary: The exact relativistic photon frequency contains an additional Lorentz factor.

methods.title: Prove common interface phase from a functional exponential identity
methods.principle: Linear independence of distinct exponential functions
steps: Require the amplitude identity at every interface point and time
Differentiate with respect to an independent coordinate
Evaluate enough derivatives to form an amplitude and wave-number system
Eliminate the nonzero amplitudes
Show the wave-number or frequency factors must coincide
Substitute back to obtain the amplitude sum
methods.boundary: Zero-amplitude waves impose no phase restriction and must be excluded when the proof assumes all amplitudes nonzero.

methods.title: Determine polarization from orthogonal wave components
methods.principle: Relative phase and amplitude of transverse oscillations
steps: Write real orthogonal components with a common phase variable
Eliminate that variable to identify the trajectory
Track increasing time at a fixed point to determine rotation sense
State the observer viewing direction
Construct the spatial snapshot separately
Relate the required source motion to the time trajectory
methods.boundary: A polarization ellipse in time and a helical spatial snapshot are not the same sketch; handedness conventions must be tied to the stated view.

methods.title: Reflect and transmit an arbitrary pulse at a nondispersive join
methods.principle: Boundary conditions on traveling profile functions
steps: Write right- and left-going arbitrary profile functions
Apply displacement and slope or force continuity at the join for every time
Express reflected and transmitted derivatives in terms of the incident derivative
Integrate with no extra constant background pulse
Rescale the transmitted spatial argument by the speed ratio
Check the time-domain boundary data
methods.boundary: This is the functional version of interface matching; the spatial width changes with speed even when the temporal pulse shape is preserved.

methods.title: Track superposed or reflected traveling pulses
methods.principle: Linear displacement superposition with translated pulse profiles
steps: Translate each original profile by its signed speed times elapsed time
For reflection construct the mirror pulse with inverted sign at a fixed end or unchanged sign at a free end
Identify overlap intervals and add signed displacements point by point
Draw every requested time with the original dimensions and consistent axes
Check fixed displacement or free-end slope at the boundary and unchanged outgoing profiles
For a finite-duration source,retain delayed reflected paths after the source stops; attenuation transfers their energy to the medium and boundaries
methods.boundary: Do not replace a rectangular pulse by a triangle or add intensities instead of signed displacement. Deriving coefficients at a finite-impedance join is an additional boundary-matching task.

methods.title: Find average force from absorbed or reflected wave momentum
methods.principle: Incident minus outgoing momentum flux
steps: Determine incident intensity and illuminated projected area
Calculate normal or vector momentum carried by each incoming and outgoing beam
Subtract outgoing momentum from incoming
Divide by area for pressure
Include the factor of two for normal perfect reflection
Compare units and limiting absorption cases

methods.title: Compare a rapidly alternating field with the response of matter
methods.principle: A material response depends on drive frequency and spatial variation,not only peak field
steps: Identify the field period and wavelength rather than treating its peak as a static field
Compare the forcing period with the relevant charge or mechanical response time
Follow the alternating force or torque and its cycle average
Distinguish suppressed slow deflection from absorbed energy or heating
Explain why multiplying a rapidly varying field by a macroscopic length is not generally a DC voltage
methods.boundary: This qualitative comparison is not a biological exposure or laser-safety assessment. Mean force or torque and mean absorbed power are different quantities.

methods.title: Read or construct a sinusoidal traveling wave
methods.principle: Constant phase propagates at omega/k; a medium particle follows local harmonic motion
steps: Identify amplitude, wave number, angular frequency and direction from data or the phase
Use lambda=2*pi/k, T=2*pi/omega and v=lambda*f
Fix the phase with the supplied displacement and direction of motion
Evaluate the wave at the requested position and time, differentiating with respect to time for particle velocity and acceleration
Read or draw spatial snapshots and time histories with their distinct axes
Select the requested next phase event and retain phase-wrap ambiguities
Across a stationary linear interface,keep the source frequency fixed by temporal continuity while allowing speed and wavelength to change
methods.boundary: Wave speed is not transverse particle speed. A spatial interval between points need not be less than one wavelength unless specified. A dispersion-law derivative or arbitrary initial-profile reconstruction adds a task.

methods.title: Choose a layer thickness or bound its transmission
methods.principle: Extrema of the coherent optical-thickness phase
steps: Use the derived layer transmission expression with actual exterior indices
Identify the coefficient and range of its oscillatory phase term
Set the phase for maximum or minimum transmission
Solve the optical-thickness condition
Choose the smallest positive thickness when required
Check reverse propagation and equal-exterior-medium special cases
methods.boundary: Half-wave resonance in equal surrounding media and quarter-wave impedance matching in unequal media are different parameter branches of the same interference condition.

methods.title: Relate longitudinal sound speed to elasticity, density or gas temperature
methods.principle: Sound speed squared is effective elastic modulus divided by mass density
steps: Select bulk modulus for a fluid or longitudinal Young modulus for a thin rod
Use v squared=B/rho or Y/rho with the actual material data
For an ideal gas use v squared=gamma*R*T/M with absolute temperature and molar mass in consistent units
Relate wavelength and transit time to speed where requested
Solve parameter ratios and distinguish material changes from unchanged-frequency transmission
methods.boundary: A bulk three-dimensional solid longitudinal speed need not equal the thin-rod Young-modulus speed. A derivation of the elastic wave equation or raw-data fit is an added task.

methods.title: Relate isotropic source power, intensity, distance and intercepted energy
methods.principle: Conserved outgoing power spreads across a spherical area
steps: Identify the isotropic point-source and negligible-loss assumptions
Use intensity=P/(solid_angle*r squared), with solid angle 4*pi for a sphere or 2*pi for a stated uniform hemisphere, or take a ratio at two radii
Multiply by projected receiving area and time for intercepted energy
Solve for power, distance or intensity and distinguish distance from change in distance
State the idealized propagation limits
